verdict.rationale: Composio's triggers system lets connected-app events (new Slack message, GitHub commit, incoming email) be pushed as structured, signed payloads to a webhook the user's app controls, which is the core building block for background automations reacting to real-world events without manual polling. However, Composio itself doesn't run or orchestrate the automation loop end-to-end (scheduling, retries, autonomous decision-making) — that logic still lives in the user's own agent/app that consumes the webhook, so 'runs autonomously in the background' is only partially delivered by Composio's infrastructure. Missing for 10: evidence of a built-in scheduler/workflow runner, autonomous multi-step execution without external orchestration, and independent confirmation that triggers reliably fire and are consumed hands-off in production.
